## This tag leaks credentials. Do not use it.

It fixes seven regressions that the 0.2.x security fixes introduced. They were found by
attacking the fixed code, on the assumption that a fix is the most likely place for the
next bug, which turned out to be correct twice over. Then its own fix for the path problem
became the next leak.

**It stays resolvable on purpose.** Deleting a tag buys nothing against an attacker, since
clones, forks and cached commit views all survive it, and it breaks anyone already pinned
here. The disclosure record is the reason to trust the current release, so it is not being
quietly dropped.

**Be precise about whose credentials leaked.** The library failed to redact ITS USERS'
secrets: a credential a caller passed into `SecretRedactor.redact` could survive the
redactor and reach the model. No credential belonging to the author has ever been in this
repository, and every credential-shaped string under `Tests/` is synthetic.

## What it fixed

- **The redactor's base64 blindness.** `/` is back in the entropy alphabet, so the AWS
  secret access key is visible to the generic pass again. Paths are excluded structurally
  instead.
- **One non-ASCII character made redaction quadratic.** A single curly apostrophe took
  296 KB from 0.030s to 1.970s, because converting `NSRange` to a Swift String range is
  O(n) on non-ASCII input. Rewritten as one forward pass: 0.049s.
- **The PEM tail leaked.** Body lines required 16 or more characters and a real key's final
  base64 line is often shorter, so the last quantum survived while the block was stamped as
  redacted.
- **The entropy floor is back to 40** after a lowering to 32 started eating ordinary
  identifiers.
- **Fence ids were silently weakened.** A caller label was filtered to its hex characters,
  so `screen-capture` became `id="ceecae"`, six guessable characters. Non-hex labels are
  hashed to full width now.
- **`tag()` missed the newest denials.** The IPv4 table grew and the tag mapping did not,
  so Oracle Cloud metadata reported as `URL_DENIED` and any alert keyed on
  `PRIVATE_NETWORK` stopped seeing it.
- **The denylist failed open for internationalized domains.** `URL.host` returns punycode
  and entries were compared raw.

## What is still wrong with it

- **The path heuristic added here discards 14% of AWS secret access keys.** It rejects any
  token carrying one segment under four characters, which base64 produces by chance.
  Measured over 200,000 random keys, rising to 34% at session-token length.
- **`64:ff9b:1::` reaches loopback.** The NAT64 local-use prefix is not decoded, so
  `URLGuard.evaluate` allows a URL that translates straight to the loopback interface.

## Breaking change

Fence ids under 16 hex characters are hashed rather than used verbatim.

## What to use instead

**0.6.1**, or at minimum 0.5.0, which is the first tag with no known credential leak. Note
that the module is `GruxKit` up to and including 0.5.0 and `Grux` from 0.6.0 onward.

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/dotcomjack/grux.git", from: "0.6.1")
.product(name: "Grux", package: "grux")
```

## Full record

The complete narrative, including the wrong first attempts, is in
[CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/dotcomjack/grux/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). The README
section [Earlier tags leak credentials](https://github.com/dotcomjack/grux#earlier-tags-leak-credentials)
lists what each of the six leaking tags does.
